subject: Re: SIG questions — data retention, prompt logs, and training policy

Subject: SIG — clarification on data retention and training on customer content

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking our SIG request. We sent the spreadsheet earlier but I wanted to call out a few high-priority items we need clarified before our legal team signs off:

1) Prompt & request logs: what is your default retention for plaintext requests and model outputs for hosted API customers? Is it possible to opt-out of retention entirely?
2) KV / in-memory caches: do you ever persist cache contents to disk or backups?
3) Use for model training: do you ever use customer prompts or generations to train or fine-tune any public or internal models? If so, what opt-in controls exist?
4) Evidence: can you provide a data retention matrix and your SOC 2 report link or evidence artifacts?

We attached our SIG to the support ticket for you to fill. Appreciate a short written response and any supporting artifacts (DPA, SOC 2) we can share with procurement.

—Maria
Maria Garcia
CISO, HealthCore

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear callouts. We filled the SIG spreadsheet and attached a short PDF summarizing the answers; below is a concise summary of the points you flagged. If you prefer, we can hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk a compliance reviewer through these.

Summary (short answers):
- Prompt & request logs:
  • Hosted API: by default, request/response logs (plaintext prompt + model output) are retained for debugging and abuse detection for up to 72 hours, after which they are deleted from hot storage. Aggregated telemetry (token counts, error rates, latency histograms) is retained for 30 days for operational analytics.
  • Customers can request extended retention up to 90 days for debugging under contract; exceptional durations are part of a dedicated or enterprise agreement.
  • Dedicated & Private deployments: we do not retain customer request/response logs in our control plane. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, runtime logs remain under customer control — Redwood does not ingest or store them unless explicitly contracted to provide hosted logging or managed services.
- KV / cache behavior:
  • KV caches used for inference are in-memory and ephemeral. We do not persist KV cache contents to disk, backups, or object storage in the hosted control plane. Cache snapshots are never used outside of the serving process.
- Use for model training:
  • Redwood does not train public models on customer proprietary prompts or outputs by default. Use of customer data for model improvements is opt-in and governed by the Data Processing Addendum (DPA). Only if a customer explicitly consents and signs an opt-in amendment will we include anonymized, scrubbed samples for model quality work.
- Evidence & artifacts:
  • Attached: redlined-sig-answers.pdf (completed SIG), retention-matrix.csv (matrix of retention windows by product), dpa-docusign-link.txt (link to standard DPA DocuSign).
  • SOC 2: our latest SOC 2 Type II report is available to customers under NDA — we can provide a secure link via the compliance portal.

Attachments: HealthCore_SIG.xlsx (filled), redlined-sig-answers.pdf (summary), retention-matrix.csv, dpa-docusign-link.txt

Next steps: tell me if the brief answers above are sufficient for your procurement team or if you want a deeper evidence pack and an on-call review with an engineer. I’m copying Ben (our security liaison) for technical follow-ups.

Thanks Ava — helpful. Two quick clarifying questions from our technical reviewer:

1) When you say hosted logs are deleted from "hot storage" after 72 hours, are there any cold backups or asynchronous replication windows that might retain copies longer? Specifically, could logs be present in backups beyond the 72-hour window?
2) For the opt-in training pathway, what controls do customers have over the sample selection and redaction process? Are we able to review samples before they are used?

Also — is there a self-serve way to export our raw request/response logs for internal audit prior to deletion?

—Security Team
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: security@healthcore.com
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG — clarification on data retention and training on customer content

Hi Maria / Security team — Ben here (Security Liaison). Quick answers below, and happy to schedule an engineer call for deeper technical detail.

1) Backups and replication: hosted request/response logs are excluded from our long-term object backups. Our ingestion pipeline writes logs to ephemeral storage zones that are not part of nightly backup snapshots. There is a short replication window (typically several minutes) for HA only; those in-flight replicas are garbage-collected and do not persist past the 72-hour retention window. We maintain audit records that an event occurred (metadata such as request id, timestamp) but not the full plaintext after deletion windows expire.

2) Training opt-in controls: customers must sign an explicit opt-in amendment to the DPA. The process includes:
  • A sample review step — customers can review and veto specific examples before they enter any training corpus.
  • Automated redaction tooling — PII detection runs on candidate samples; customers can provide additional redaction rules.
  • Data minimization — only minimal context needed for the quality task is included.

3) Raw export: we provide a secure, time-limited export for customers (S3 presigned download) for the retention window if they request it. Exports are only available while data still exists in the window (e.g., within 72 hours for default hosted logs). For Dedicated customers we can enable longer-lived exports as part of a contractual configuration.

Attachments included again: retention-matrix.csv and DPA DocuSign link.

If useful, I can set up a 30-minute call with one of our infra engineers to demonstrate the export flow and answer questions about backup exclusion. When are you available?

Thanks,
